Settled 2026-11-16, from the senior review's first item ("the numeric core
exists three times and disagrees with itself").

- **`curve_lab/measure.py` is the only exact implementation** of grid, bend,
  arc, inflections and closest. `scripts/ph_quintic_metrics.py` is now a facade
  over it, keeping the names a dozen scripts import. Reason: two
  implementations agreed on 74 curves and disagreed on the seventy-fifth —
  `loop-13-15-17-mid-1`, exact grid 36, page 5,148 — and a third copy would
  have found a seventy-sixth.
- **The disagreement is a double limit, not a coding slip.** The page scales a
  row to whole numbers and squares it; a coefficient of 1.03e8 squares to
  1.06e16, past 9.0e15 where a double stops counting by ones. No amount of
  care in the JavaScript fixes that; the exact answer has to be carried.
- **A stored curve's numbers come from its record.** The record now holds the
  exact grid and bend, and the page prints them, labelled "(exact, from the
  record)", while the loaded rows are still untouched. The first edit returns
  the page to its own arithmetic, which is honest for a curve being made.
  Reason: the page must not claim an exactness it does not have, and a record
  must not be re-derived by a viewer.
- **`scripts/exact_numbers.py` audits every record against the core**, and
  `--write` puts the exact number back. `tests/test_exact_numbers.py` runs the
  audit in the suite, so a wrong number is a red test, not a curve that looks
  different from its figure.

## Exact form before cubics — 2026-11-17

Settled 2026-11-17, by the operator: "i am trying to avoid cubic beziers until
later... that is the last step before transfer to inkscape and glyphs 4".

- **The working representation is exact polynomial data** — the speed pair, the
  position polynomials, or a ratio of two polynomials. A cubic Bézier chain is
  the **export step** (PLAN S5), not the form the work is reasoned in. A card
  may print a cubic fit's measured miss as a number; it does not draw the cubic
  chain.
- **A PH curve's offset is exact and rational**: `O = C + d·(−y', x')/σ`, with
  `σ = u² + v²` a polynomial. `curve_lab/ph_offset.py` implements it in
  `Fraction`; there is no Bézier control data and no weight in the card.
- **Measured on `integer-105`** (`u = 2 − 5t + 6t²`, `v = 4 − 20t + 20t² − 2t³`):
  pitch 105, and at 105 the curve has exactly **two** lattice points, the ends.
  The first interior hit is the midpoint at **t = 1/2, grid 3360** — 32 times
  the pitch. The next stations are 25,515 (t = 1/3), 76,545 (t = 2/3), 143,360
  (t = 3/4) and so on, one at a time.
- **A rail hits the lattice only when d is chosen for the hit.** At
  d = 41/1120 the rail's first hit is the same grid 3360, at the same t; at
  d = 3/100 it is 688,800. The reason is arithmetic: the unit normal at the
  station is (40/41, −9/41), so d must carry the factor 41. A branch is its own
  curve, not a parallel offset, so it can be built on the lattice independently
  — the rails are the only side curves whose hits are dictated by the parent.
- **A station is not a mirror line.** The midpoint station translates to
  (0, 4130) on grid 3360, and the two rails land at (120, 4103) and
  (−120, 4157). But the curve is not symmetric (half-turn gap 37% of its size,
  vertical-mirror gap 49%), the tangent at the station is 12.7° off vertical,
  the inflection is at t = 0.5051, and x = 0 meets the curve four times. A true
  mirror axis needs a symmetric curve: the Pythagorean integer cubic family is
  half-turn symmetric with its midpoint at (c, 0) on scale 1, but it is not PH,
  so its rail is fitted. A symmetric PH curve is the third option.
- **A symmetric PH candidate was found** (2026-11-17, **not adopted**):
  `u = 1`, `v = (2t − 1)²`. Both speeds are even about 1/2, so the curve is a
  half turn about its midpoint (2/5, 1/3), the tangent there is exactly
  horizontal, and the vertical line through it crosses the curve once. Grid 15
  puts the station at (6, 5); one shift by −2/5 puts it at (0, 5); both rails at
  d = 1/15 land at (0, 6) and (0, 4) on the same grid; the + rail's first
  interior hit is grid 5. It is the first curve here with both an exact rail and
  a mirror station, and it changes the primary curve, so the choice is the
  operator's.

## Browser JS, Node as a tool — 2026-11-17

Settled 2026-11-17, by the operator: the page layer should be JS, but "dont get
too dependent on node except for good reason (the code is already debugged)".

- **Live page maths is JS**, in small self-contained modules that load as a
  plain script or through `require`; no bundler, under 200 lines each.
- **Node is a verification tool**, not a build dependency: it runs the browser
  modules' tests and the Playwright page checks. No generator moves to Node to
  be Node.
- **Python stays where it is debugged** — the engine, the records, the audits,
  the generators that write static cards. A calculation moves only when a page
  must compute it live, and then the Python twin is deleted in the same commit.
- **One number, one source**: a live number from the JS module, a stored number
  from the record. No third implementation.
- **No floats on an exact path**; the 1e16 case (`loop-13-15-17-mid-1`) is the
  mandatory test when a grid or crossing function moves.
- The first slice: `exact.js`, `poly_exact.js`, `ph_offset.js`, pinned to the
  Python numbers by `tests/js/ph_offset.test.js`; `scripts/test.py` runs
  `node --test`; `scripts/code_count.sh` prints the language split at handoff.
  The full plan and order is `state/PORT-int.md`.

## Book plates — 2026-11-17

The short-term deliverable: PNG plates for a book, SVGs kept beside them for the
later Inkscape step. The operator's rules, in their words: **white background,
no text on the image, clipped to the edge of the curve**, a plain gallery with
no input fields.

- **This overrides the figure-label rule for these plates.** A book plate has no
  title, axes or legend inside the image; the gallery and the manifest carry the
  name and the note. Every other figure still follows the label rule.
- **The name is `<descriptor>-<variant>-t-exp-c-<serial>`**, for example
  `swan-1-t-exp-c-0001`. The serial is allocated once in `book/plates.json` and
  never reused, so a re-export keeps the name and a LibreOffice link survives.
- **The size is decided by the bounding box of spine plus both rails.** The
  canvas aspect is that box, so the curve fills 97.6% of the long side; a margin
  of 1.2% keeps the stroke from being cut. Long side 3000 px, stroke 0.35% of
  it, 300 dpi in the PNG so LibreOffice inserts at 254 mm rather than 790 mm.
- **The rails are character rails, not parallel offsets** (operator,
  2026-11-17): a ±d base at the record's width percent, bowed by its `plus` /
  `minus` strength and its `bow`, `s` or `taper` profile. The construction is
  the sandbox's (`workbench/ph_nth_panels.js`, `characterRail`), reproduced in
  `workbench/plate_math.js`. A parallel rail is a later feature and is not
  drawn. When the base offset would fold, the width is halved; at the 0.2%
  floor the plate is spine-only and says so.
- **The inline data is checked.** The lab's curve data is written into the page;
  the generator refuses an empty list, a count mismatch or a row of zeros, and a
  test compares the inline copy with the file. Reason: the 2026-11-16 fault, when
  a damaged read emptied two thirds of the saved curves.
- **A folded base offset is never drawn.** If `|d·κ|` at the record's width
  would fold, the width is halved until it does not; at the 0.2% floor the
  plate is spine-only and the caption says so. Two of the 27 saved curves land
  there: `involute-fit` and `inflect-2`.

## Starring is a download, not a server write — 2026-11-17

The operator stars designs in the lab and wants them in the book gallery. The
lab runs in the browser; its stars live in `localStorage`; the exporter runs in
Node and cannot read a browser. The bridge is a **downloaded file**:
`workbench/starred.json`. The lab allocates each star a serial (from 0301) once,
stores it with the settings, and downloads the file; the exporter reads it if
present and adds the plates under the top section. There is no write endpoint on
the server, and a missing file is a prompt, not an error. This is the same
pattern as the saved-curve list: the browser cannot be the database.

## Symmetry is measured, not guessed — 2026-11-17

The operator's note: the saved curves are not all internally symmetric, so the
lab groups them. The measurement is on the spine, at 400 stations:

- **half turn** — `C(1/2+s) + C(1/2−s) = 2C(1/2)`;
- **mirror** — the same about the vertical line through the midpoint, so the
  x values add to `2x(1/2)` and the y values are equal;
- **none** — neither, within 0.5% of the bounding-box diagonal.

**The operator's category is stricter than the axis test.** Among the seed,
only `u-bowl` and `wave-coarse` count as symmetric; the 60 **found** curves take
their measured symmetry. The measured kind stays in the data and the readout
prints both, so the difference is visible: `v-sharp` is a measured mirror but
the operator's category is asymmetric. The lab now offers **88 curves**
(28 seed/new + 60 found) and **62 are symmetric** under this rule. The record
lives in `workbench/real-curves.json`, with `source` (seed, new, found),
`symmetry` and `category` per curve.

## Central designs are at least two curves — 2026-11-17

The operator's definition: a central design has **at least two curves joined at
their legs** (or end to end). Two forms so far:

- **The leaf** — curve a below, the flipped curve b above, both pairs of feet on
  the same two points. Measured tip angles: arch/arch 90°/90°, S/arch 90°/0°.
- **The chain** — curve a then curve b, end to end, **not flipped**. A shallow-leg
  curve and a steep-leg curve can meet at a shared foot; the join angle is the
  difference between a's end tangent and b's start tangent. That difference is
  the design's decision, not a fault: it is a corner unless the angles match.
- The book plates are single curves (spine plus character rails), not central
  designs.

## Square and frame: the leg bisects the corner — 2026-11-17

The operator's construction, 2026-11-17: measure the curve's chord (the
end-to-end distance on x, with the legs at the same y), make an invisible square
of that side, and put one curve on each edge. North is the x-flip, east the
quarter turn, west the mirror. `curve_lab/square_assembly.py` and
`workbench/plate_math.js` implement it; `scripts/square_try.py` is the static
proof and `workbench/square-frame.html` is the lab.

- **One rule: the leg bisects the corner.** A square corner is 90°, so the leg
  is 45°. The angle is reached by scaling the curve *across its chord*, so the
  ends stay on the edge and the square stays closed at the measured side.
- **Measured joins:** an arch at a 45° leg joins continuously (0° kink); an S
  at 45° joins at 90° (a miter); an arch as drawn leaves 16°.
- **The frame is the same rule with `n` chords a side.** The side is
  `n × the chord`, so 3 copies fill one side and 5 make a finer, lace-like
  scale. The frame and the central cross are built **separately** and only
  overlaid — a picture in a frame. Do not merge them into one curve set.
- **The page is a lab, not a plate.** Curve, curves per side, leg angle, print
  size, fill, alternate flips and the cross, all live. The page measures in
  points (1/72 in).
- **The stroke floor is exactly 1 point** at every size from 1 to 4 inches:
  `strokeFor` returns `max(1, 0.0035 × width in points)`, so the percentage
  rules above 3.97 in and the floor holds below it. A scaled-down plate never
  loses its line.
- **Squares and rectangles only, for now.** The operator parked other polygons
  on 2026-11-17. The same corner rule holds when they return: a pentagon's
  corner is 108° (leg 54°), a pentagram point 36° (leg 18°) — but the box is
  not square and the counts are per axis, so it is a separate piece of work.

## Astro is the app — 2026-11-17

Settled 2026-11-17, by the operator: the final result is Astro; no React; local
file support; it must work on Next and other servers. `app/` runs Astro 5.18.2
with the Node adapter on **:4321**. Astro 7 was refused by this machine's Node
22.4.1 (it wants >=22.23.4); Astro 5 accepts it, and a global 5.18.2 is
installed. The page imports `workbench/plate_math.js` and
`workbench/real-curves.json` — no second maths. The save is
`app/src/lib/stars.js`, plain Node (validate, temp file, rename), called by a
thin Astro route; a Next or Hono route can call the same function. The lab's
"save to workbench" writes `workbench/starred.json` from the page, and the
download stays as the fallback. Migration order and the Python bridge are in
`state/ASTRO-int.md`. The old generated pages remain until each is ported and
deleted in the same commit.

## The book gallery is the Astro page — 2026-11-17

Settled 2026-11-17, when A2 landed. The generated `book/index.html` is retired.

- **The gallery is a server page**, `app/src/pages/book.astro`, reading
  `book/plates.json` and `workbench/starred.json` on every request. Reason: a
  star saved to `workbench/starred.json` shows up without a rebuild, and the
  listing cannot drift from the file the way a generated page can.
- **One caption, one module.** `workbench/plate_compose.js` holds the compose
  call; the exporter and the gallery both require it. Reason: the caption is
  the plate's name in the book, so two copies of the wording is the fault class
  the register already names.
- **Every star is listed, even before its PNG exists.** A star with no exported
  plate says `PNG not exported yet` on its card. Reason: dropping it would make
  the gallery quietly disagree with the file it claims to list.
- **The PNGs are served from `book/plates/`**, not copied into `app/public/`:
  `app/src/pages/api/plate/[id].js` checks the id against the plate-name pattern
  and the resolved path against the plate directory. Reason: 5.8 MB of plates
  would otherwise exist twice, and two copies drift.
- **The exporter writes SVG, PNG and `render.html` only.** No page is generated
  from it. A missing `starred.json` is still a prompt, not an error.

## Searching and naming

- **Symmetry is built in by choosing roots, never by hoping.** A row from
  mirrored roots is symmetric by construction; a random small-integer row
  essentially never is (1,500 draws, 0 hits).
- **Names state the construction**: kind + every mirrored pair + the middle
  count. `lace-1of9-3` = a lace (four or more self-crossings), pair at 1/9 and
  8/9, three roots at 1/2. `2x` marks a repeated pair. Settled.
- **The finds are split by batch.** Part 2 keeps the earlier family; the
  experimental page's foot carries only the newer batch, tangliest first, odd
  shapes included. Reason: a page for looking at new shapes should not be a
  second copy of the kept collection. `found-curves.json` marks each row
  `batch: first` or `batch: new`. Settled 2026-11-14, by the operator.
- **The "x row roots" axis turned out to be the bow, sampled finer.** A row like
  `[7, -25, 25]` is `7(1 - 3.57 t(1-t))`, a bow of 3.57 — between the old
  hand-picked 2 and 4. So the gain came from trying bow strengths that were not
  on the list, not from a new construction. The bow slider now reaches ±12 for
  that reason.
- **Finds land in `workbench/found-curves.json`**, which the galleries read at
  load. A row proportional to an existing seed is skipped.

## Process

- **No internet, no CI, no push without the operator saying so.**
- **Generated pages may be read.** Reading the built page is how a claim about
  the page is checked; the DOM is the evidence, not the generator's list.
- **A number in a report is measured, not recalled.** Counts, positions and
  order come from the DOM or from a script's printed output, with the command
  named.


<!-- source: state/REGRESSIONS-int.md -->

# REGRESSIONS-int — fixed bugs, and the check that keeps them fixed

A bug fixed twice is a process failure. This file is the register: one row per
fault that cost real work, the test that now guards it, and the date it was
fixed. The tests live in `tests/test_regressions.py` and run in the fast suite.

**The rule, for every session:**

1. **Never delete a row or its test** because a change made it awkward. That is
   the moment the test is earning its keep.
2. **A fix and its row land in the same commit.** A fix without a test is not
   finished.
3. **If a test fails and the new behaviour is right**, the row is amended in the
   same commit, with the reason written down — never silently.
4. Before a handoff: `.venv/bin/python -m unittest tests.test_regressions`.

## The register

| # | date | the fault, as the operator saw it | the check | what it protects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-11-14 | "when I refresh, it defaults to an incorrect curve because the values get put directly, not in the correct whole power boxes" | `test_a_power_lands_in_its_own_box_not_the_next_one` | power→box placement in `curve_records.rows_for_step` |
| 2 | 2026-11-14 | "why don't I see any .5 roots? you messed something up" | `test_the_half_power_boxes_are_never_removed_by_the_starter` | the experimental page always opens at step ½ |
| 3 | 2026-11-14 | rows and powers disagreed; two sources of truth | `test_stored_curves_keep_terms_and_drop_flat_rows` | the `curve-lab.curves/2` format |
| 4 | 2026-11-14 | "is this the page I am looking at?" — stale copies looked like broken pages | `test_the_build_stamp_sits_at_the_foot_and_is_current` | the footer build stamp |
| 5 | 2026-11-14 | "there should be about double the number of sliders" — the decade slider vanished | `test_every_speed_number_still_has_two_sliders` | mantissa + decade per number |
| 6 | 2026-11-14 | step ½ could not reach `t^7` | `test_the_ladder_still_reaches_thirty_numbers` | the 30-number ladder |
| 7 | 2026-11-14 | "it shows the curve, and then the curve again in a box" | `test_an_open_gallery_cell_draws_one_curve_only` | one figure per open cell |
| 8 | 2026-11-14 | "figures 1-6 are obviously wrong" — the section re-shuffled itself | `test_the_knotlike_section_still_opens_with_the_operators_curves` | the operator's six first |
| 9 | 2026-11-14 | position-based ordering drifted when a curve was added | `test_the_ordering_rules_name_curves_rather_than_positions` | order stated by name |
| 10 | 2026-11-14 | a grid and inflection count claimed for fractional powers | `test_a_fractional_step_reports_no_grid_and_no_inflection_count` | honest readouts |
| 11 | 2026-11-14 | no number to steer "make the knot bigger" by | `test_the_readout_still_reports_knot_and_leg_shares` | knot/leg shares |
| 12 | 2026-11-14 | loading a curve silently changed the exponent step | `test_loading_a_curve_does_not_change_the_exponent_step` | the step belongs to the operator |
| 13 | 2026-11-14 | "Build from flat spots is putting the numbers in the wrong boxes when I click the button" | `test_the_flat_spots_fill_whole_power_boxes` | the fill places coefficients by power |
| 14 | 2026-11-14 | "both rows: 1 + size(t - t2)" went lopsided | `check-nth-page.mjs` (exp page: gap stays 0.0000) | the product keeps its tail instead of trimming it |
| 15 | 2026-11-14 | undo after a rung grew crashed a box | `check-nth-page.mjs` (exp page: undo runs clean) | restored rows are padded to the boxes that exist |
| 16 | 2026-11-14 | "a fraction like 1/4 ... .1 doesnt seem like the way" — 1/3 blew the grid to 8.7e13 | `test_the_tweak_sizes_are_binary_exact_only` | only binary-exact sizes are offered |
| 17 | 2026-11-14 | "fix these buttons so they never lose data" — a lower rung deleted the higher numbers | `check-nth-page.mjs` (rung round trip keeps 777) | rung changes stash coefficients instead of deleting them |
| 18 | 2026-11-14 | the suite went red on `ph-nth-sandbox.html` with nothing changed: the reproduce check compared the build stamp, so it failed whenever the minute rolled over | `test_the_generator_reproduces_the_page` (compares after dropping the `n-build` line) | the rebuild check tests the page, not the clock |
| 19 | 2026-11-14 | 172 errors in `test_ph_root_found.py` for hours: the test read `speedX`/`bend`/`pitch` while `found-curves.json` had become `curve-lab.curves/2` with `terms`/`measured` | `test_the_walk_landed_something` (asserts the format) and the rows rebuilt from `terms` | the found-curves checks follow the file format, so a format change cannot silently orphan them |
| 20 | 2026-11-14 | "the page should have a gallery" — the experimental page had one, and its test still demanded none, so the suite stayed red | `test_the_page_keeps_the_gallery` | the experimental page keeps its gallery; the reversed guard is written in the test's docstring |
| 21 | 2026-11-16 | "grid 1/5,148 against the record's 1/36, with identical rows" — the page's doubles squared a row of 10^8 (1.06e16, past 2^53) and counted the grid 143 times too big | `test_exact_numbers.py`: `test_every_stored_curve_agrees_with_the_exact_core`, `test_the_large_row_keeps_grid_36_not_the_page_5148`, `test_the_page_squares_the_same_row_wrong_and_is_told_not_to` | one exact core (`curve_lab/measure.py`), the record as the authority for a stored curve, and the page printing the record's number while its rows are untouched |
| 22 | 2026-11-16 | "the list said HANDOFF was 2,226 lines when it was 2,353, and the counter said 'counts already right'" — the row pattern expected the file name second, so every numbered Tier 0 row was skipped | `tests/test_reading_counts.py`: `test_a_numbered_row_is_one_the_counter_recognises`, `test_the_pairing_has_no_stale_count_left` | the reading list's counts, and the counter that must refresh them |
| 23 | 2026-11-16 | "how can you lose all those curves when we werent even touching that code" — a damaged read became an empty list, and the next save wrote one curve over all of them | `scripts/check-saved.mjs` (six browser checks: seeding, repair from backup, no wipe after a bad read, load from a restored button, a pair record) and `tests/test_operator_list.py` (the list on disk is current and complete) | the saved-curve buttons: no write after a failed read, a backup and mirror on every save, and a file to seed a reset browser |
| 24 | 2026-11-16 | the page said `crosses itself 5` for `lace-1of10-1of5-3` and the record said 4 — the stored numbers predated the parameter-pair dedupe | `tests/test_crossings.py`: every record matches the router, the triple point counts as three pairs, and the count is scale-free | 100 stale crossing counts, and the one definition they now share |

## Fixed and measured, but not yet in the fast suite

These have browser-level proof in `scripts/check-nth-page.mjs` (which needs a
headless browser), so they are named here rather than duplicated:

- the flat-spot strip: click to add, click a dot to remove one copy (three clicks
  at ½ give a count of 3);
- the suggestion list fills the known row `[-8, 129, -663, 1522, -1620, 648]`;
- typing in a speed box keeps its sign and its decimal point;
- the gallery loads a curve into the sandbox with the rows it was saved with;
- the saved-curve buttons survive a damaged value and a browser reset
  (`scripts/check-saved.mjs`: six checks, seeded from `workbench/operator-list.json`).

## Known open faults

- `cut and rebuild` (arc length) falls back to the whole curve on every curve
  tried: the span needed is longer than the largest exact square below 1, so
  only the whole span keeps the numbers exact. It reports this rather than
  cutting silently.
- `rebuild without the legs` is exact and verified against a Python reference,
  but the crossings on these curves span nearly all of `t`, so it usually has
  nothing to remove.
- The percentage-of-`t` control added earlier is superseded and inert; the
  markup is gone, the handler remains harmless.


<!-- source: state/DATA-int.md -->

# DATA-int — the datasets, their formats, and who touches them

Solo user, one machine. The store is files in git; there is no database and no
migration path, by the operator's decision on 2026-11-17. What makes it safe is
that every file says what it is, one loader reads it, and one check fails when
that stops being true.

## The contract

1. **Every JSON dataset under `workbench/` is an object with a `format` line**
   (`name/version`), as the first key. A list-shaped file is not allowed: give
   it `{"format": ..., "curves": [...]}` so it can grow a version later.
2. **One loader**, `curve_lab/datafile.py:load(path, expected)`. It refuses a
   missing file, bad JSON, no format, or the wrong format. Read through it, never
   with a bare `json.load`, when the caller cares whether the file is sound.
3. **One registry**, `FORMATS` in `curve_lab/datafile.py`. A dataset not in the
   table is not real: the formatter will not stamp it and the audit will not
   check it. `state/DATA-int.md` is the same list for a reader; a test keeps the
   two in step.

```sh
.venv/bin/python scripts/data_format.py --check   # is every file stamped?
.venv/bin/python scripts/data_format.py --write   # stamp what is missing (one line each)
.venv/bin/python scripts/data_audit.py            # read every file through the loader
```

`data_format.py` inserts the line after the opening brace, keeping the file's
own indentation, so the diff is one line per file. It refuses to write a file
that would not parse. Tests: `tests/test_data_audit.py`.

**When a generator rewrites a stamped file without the `format` line**, the suite
fails at `data_format.py --check`. Fix the generator (add the key first in the
document it builds) rather than re-stamping by hand, or the next run repeats it.
`ph_quintic_presets`, `ph_quintic_yours` and `septic_curves` were fixed this way
on 2026-11-17; their tests compare the written file with the generator, so they
would fail either way. The other generators are fixed on first failure.

## The datasets

Rows are counted by `data_audit.py` (2026-11-17).

| file | format | kind | written by | read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `family-census.json` | `curve-lab.family-census/1` | cache | `scripts/curve_files.py` | `scripts/family_census.py` |
| `flowers.json` | `curve-lab.flowers/1` | cache | `scripts/stems_print.py` | `scripts/stems_print.py` |
| `finder.json` | `curve-lab.finder/1` | cache | `scripts/curve_finder.py` | the Astro `/finder` page |
| `finder.backup.json` | `curve-lab.finder/1` | backup | the `/finder` page, on save | `readSaved()` repair, then the page |
| `finder-stars.json` | `curve-lab.finder-stars/1` | record | `app/src/lib/finder-stars.js` | the star list on the `/finder` page |
| `finder-stars.backup.json` | `curve-lab.finder-stars/1` | backup | the `/finder` page, on save | `readSaved()` repair, then the page |
| `found-curves.json` | `curve-lab.curves/2` | record | `scripts/real_curves.mjs` | the galleries, `ph_nth_panels.js` |
| `found-for-exp.json` | `curve-lab.curves/2` | orphan | — | — (no reader; archive when the public tree is cut) |
| `g3-catalogue-cache.json` | `curve-lab.g3-catalogue-cache/1` | cache | `scripts/g3_catalogue.py` | `scripts/g3_catalogue.py` |
| `g3-catalogue.json` | `curve-lab.g3-catalogue/1` | record | `scripts/g3_catalogue.py` | `scripts/g3_gate.py`, `g3_cubic_native.py` |
| `g3-diagnostics.json` | `curve-lab.g3-diagnostics/1` | cache | `scripts/g3_handover.py` | `scripts/recheck.py` |
| `g3-handover.json` | `curve-lab.g3-handover/1` | cache | `scripts/g3_handover.py` | `scripts/g3_showcase_doc.py` |
| `manifest.json` | `curve-lab.manifest/1` | index | `scripts/hub.py` | the Astro hub, `scripts/hub.py` |
| `moved-curves.json` | `curve-lab.moved/1` | record | `scripts/moved_notes.py` | `scripts/operator_list.py` |
| `operator-list.json` | `curve-lab.operator-list/1` | record | `scripts/operator_list.py` | the lab's seed list, `tests/test_operator_list.py` |
| `ph-11th-fitted-curves.json` | `curve-lab.ph-fitted/1` | cache | `scripts/ph_11th_sandbox2.py` | part 2 of the sandbox |
| `ph-fitted-curves.json` | `curve-lab.ph-fitted/1` | cache | `scripts/ph_fit_showcase.py` | `scripts/ph_nth_sandbox2.py` |
| `ph-quintic-presets.json` | `curve-lab.ph-quintic-presets/1` | cache | `scripts/ph_quintic_gallery.py` | the quintic gallery |
| `ph-quintic-yours.json` | `curve-lab.ph-quintic-yours/1` | cache | `scripts/ph_quintic_yours.py` | the quintic gallery |
| `real-curves.json` | `real-curves/1` | record | `scripts/real_curves.mjs` | the lab, the book, `plate_math.js` |
| `root-family.json` | `curve-lab.root-family/1` | cache | `scripts/ph_root_search.py` | `scripts/ph_root_search.py` |
| `septic-curves.json` | `curve-lab.septic-curves/1` | cache | `scripts/ph_11th_sandbox.py` | the septic sandbox |
| `septic-samples.json` | `curve-lab.septic-samples/1` | cache | `scripts/septic_samples.py` | `scripts/ph_septic_sandbox.py` |
| `starred.json` | `starred/1` | runtime | `POST /api/stars` (`app/src/lib/stars.js`) | the Astro book gallery |

**Record** means the file is the authority for a number the site shows.
**Cache** means it is derived and can be rebuilt by its script. **Runtime** means
a running page writes it. **Orphan** means nothing reads it.

## The runtime file

`workbench/starred.json` is **tracked**, seeded with an empty `starred/1` object,
and overwritten by the save endpoint when the operator stars a design. The write
is atomic and validated (`app/src/lib/stars.js`); git is the backup. Commit it
after a save if the stars matter to the next session — nothing does that
automatically, by design: the page must not need git to save.

## Known oddities, recorded not fixed

- `found-for-exp.json` (168 rows) has no writer and no reader.
- `ph-11th-fitted-curves.json` and `ph-fitted-curves.json` are the same size and
  row count under the same format; they may be duplicates. Not merged, because
  two different sandboxes name them.
- `starred.json` is empty today: no stars have been saved to disk yet.


<!-- source: state/PORT-int.md -->

# PORT-int — browser JS, Node where it earns it, Python where it is debugged

The operator's position, 2026-11-17: **the page layer should be JS**, but do not
get dependent on Node for its own sake, and **do not rewrite code that is already
debugged**. This file turns that into a rule with a boundary, so the same
argument is not had again.

## The rule

1. **The browser is the product, so live maths is JS.** A number a control, a
   slider or a readout computes at load comes from a JS module the page loads.
2. **Node is a verification tool, not a build dependency.** It runs the browser
   modules' tests (`node --test`) and the Playwright page checks. No page
   generator moves to Node just to be Node.
3. **Python stays where it is debugged** — the engine (`curve_lab/`), the stored
   records, the audits, and the page generators that write static cards.
4. **Move a calculation only when the page must compute it live.** A static card
   may keep the Python-computed record; it does not need a second implementation
   in the browser.
5. **One number, one source.** A live number comes from the JS module; a stored
   number comes from the record. Never a third.
6. **No floats on an exact path.** `floatSampler` is for drawing only. Any
   lattice, grid or crossing answer is `Rational`/`BigInt`, and the 1e16 case
   that broke doubles is a mandatory test when such a function moves.

## What moved on 2026-11-17

| file | lines | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `workbench/exact.js` | 100 | `Rational` on `BigInt`: normalise, add/sub/mul/div, compare, integer check |
| `workbench/poly_exact.js` | 80 | coefficient lists low-to-high: add, multiply, integrate, derivative, evaluate |
| `workbench/ph_offset.js` | 129 | the PH curve, the exact offset, lattice scale, first interior hit, hits at a scale |
| `tests/js/ph_offset.test.js` | 85 | pinned to the Python numbers: polynomials, normal equations, grid 3360, rail grids, the symmetric candidate |

The gate is `scripts/test.py`: after the Python modules it runs `node --test
tests/js` and prints the pass/fail count (8 pass, ~0.3 s). `scripts/test.py`
remains the one command; no second gate.

Sizes: every module above is under 200 lines, has one job, and loads either as a
plain script (`globalThis.Exact`) or through `require`. That is the house shape
for JS modules: no bundler, no import graph to debug.

## What is deliberately not moving

- **`curve_lab/measure.py`** (293 lines). It is the debugged exact core, and the
  pages display its stored numbers. It moves only if a live control needs grid,
  bend, arc, inflection or closest; then that one function moves, with a parity
  test over every stored record.
- **The 123 page generators.** They are the 49k, and they work. A generator is
  replaced only when its page's maths moves live, and then the `.py` is deleted
  in the same commit.
- **`web/server.py`** (329 lines, Cloud Run image). A deploy decision, not a
  curve decision. It can be the last Python process in the repo.

## Next fruit, in order

1. **`workbench/rail_chart.js`** — the labelled-figure helper for the rail lab.
   The Python `rail_chart.py` is its twin until the page moves live.
2. **The rail lab controls** — the page reads `ph_offset.js` at load for the
   offset, the lattice grid and the station; the generator writes only the
   shell and the prose. This is the page that proves the shape.
3. **Crossings in JS** — small and pure, needed if a lab control reports a live
   crossing count. Parity against `scripts/ph_crossings.py` on the stored
   records.
4. **Grid and bend in JS** — only with the 1e16 guard and the full-record parity
   test. Do not start until a page needs them live.
5. **`measure.py` last**, and the generators on touch.
6. **The server never**, unless the deploy changes for another reason.

## The measure of progress

Run at every handoff:

```sh
sh scripts/code_count.sh
```

August 2026 baseline (2026-11-17): Python 67,062 lines (engine 8,027 · scripts
48,916 · tests 9,790 · web 329), our JS 11,951 (workbench 5,527 · scripts 6,424).
The target is not zero Python. It is: **no new page maths in Python, and the
Python count flat or falling at each handoff.** A handoff that raises the Python
count must say why in one line.

## Risks, named

- **BigInt is slower than Fraction is on CPython for this arithmetic.** The
  q ≤ 40 search is 35 ms in Node; a q ≤ 200 search was not timed and must be
  measured before a page depends on it.
- **Float creep.** JS makes `number` the easy path; the exact path must stay
  explicit. The tests reject a float passed to `Rational.from`.
- **Two implementations during a move.** A moved function is two implementations
  until the Python twin is deleted; that window is one commit, not one release.
- **The 1e16 case.** `loop-13-15-17-mid-1`: a coefficient of 1.03e8 squares past
  2^53. Any JS grid answer that does not carry it is wrong by 143×.

## What is not decided

Whether the rail lab replaces `integer-ph-rail.html` or sits beside it, and
whether the Python chart survives. Those follow from the lab's first version,
not from this plan.


<!-- source: app/README.md -->

# The Astro app

Astro 5.18 with `@astrojs/node`, on **http://localhost:4321**.

- **`/` is the hub:** every page the app will use, live in one scroll — the lab
  and the book gallery first, then the 86 workbench pages by intent, then any
  workbench HTML the manifest does not name. The shell is an admin-dashboard
  layout (fixed sidebar, top bar, card grid); the colours and type are
  curve-lab's own. `src/lib/pages.js` builds the list from
  `../workbench/manifest.json` plus the files on disk.
- **Workbench pages are served, not copied:** `src/pages/pages/[...file].js`
  reads `../workbench/<file>` (with a path check) so a preview is always the
  current generated page.
- **Shell credit:** the hub's layout — fixed sidebar, top bar, card grid — follows
  the Flowbite Astro admin dashboard (MIT, Bergside). No Tailwind, Flowbite or
  template code is used; the CSS here is ours.
- **`/lab` is the lab; `/book` is the book gallery.** The lab page is ported; its
  stars are saved by the page itself to `workbench/starred.json`.

- **Why 5.18, not 7:** this machine's Node is 22.4.1; Astro 7 needs >=22.23.4.
  Astro 5 supports >=22.0. A **global Astro 5.18.2** is installed; Astro still
  needs the adapter (`@astrojs/node`) local to each project, so the shared thing
  is the version and the CLI, not one `node_modules` for every folder.
- **Shared code:** `../workbench/plate_math.js` and `../workbench/real-curves.json`
  through Vite's `server.fs.allow`; one copy of the maths and the data.
- **The design is remembered:** the lab writes its controls to
  `localStorage` (`square-lab-state`) on every change and restores them on load,
  so reopening the tab returns the design on screen, not just the page.
- **The save:** `src/lib/stars.js` is plain Node (atomic write, validated ids);
  `src/pages/api/stars.js` is a thin adapter. A Next route handler or a Hono
  route can import the same function.
- **The book gallery:** `/book` (`src/pages/book.astro`) lists the starred
  plates from `../workbench/starred.json`, then the cross and leaf from
  `../book/plates.json`, then the singles. `src/lib/gallery.js` reads both files
  on every request and takes each caption from `../workbench/plate_compose.js`,
  the same call the exporter makes. The PNGs are served by
  `src/pages/api/plate/[id].js` from `../book/plates/`, so nothing is copied.
  The generated `book/index.html` is gone.
- **The endpoint:** `POST /api/stars` with `{ "plates": [...] }` wrote
  `workbench/starred.json` in the test run.

```sh
cd app && npm run dev      # http://localhost:4321
npm test                   # the save tests, no browser
```

Not ported yet: the other workbench pages (the hub previews them from the
Python-generated files). The old lab at
`:8003` stays until the Astro page reaches parity.


<!-- source: book/README.md -->

# book — temporary plate export

The short-term deliverable: PNG plates for a book, from the curves we already
have. SVGs are written beside them, so the later Inkscape step starts from the
same geometry. The operator's rules, 2026-11-17: **white ground, no text on the
image, clipped to the curve**, a plain gallery with no controls.

## The name

    <descriptor>-<variant>-t-exp-c-<serial>

    swan-1-t-exp-c-0001.png

- **descriptor** — the shape's word: `swan`, `sweep`, `lace`. Lowercase letters
  and digits, no hyphen (the `-t-exp-c-` marker is how the name is parsed).
- **variant** — an integer, for another offset or another member of the family.
- **t** — temporary set. The final set can be `f` without renaming the geometry.
- **exp** — export, not a working page.
- **c** — curve (as opposed to a terminal or an ornament).
- **serial** — four digits, allocated once in `plates.json`, never reused. A
  re-export keeps the name, so a LibreOffice link survives.

## The image

| property | value | why |
|---|---|---|
| long side | 3000 px | 10 in at 300 dpi; downscaling for the page is safe |
| dpi | 300 (PNG `pHYs`) | LibreOffice inserts at 254 × the aspect mm, not 790 mm |
| ground | `#ffffff` | print |
| ink | `#111111` | print |
| stroke | 0.35% of the long side (10.5 px) | about 0.5 mm at 150 mm wide |
| rails | **character rails**: a ±d base at `width%` of the spine's size, bowed by the record's `plus`/`minus` and `bow`/`s`/`taper` profile | the sandbox's character, not a parallel offset |
| margin | 1.2% of the long side (36 px) | the stroke is never cut; the curve fills 97.6% |
| text | none | operator's instruction; the gallery carries the name |
| gallery | two columns, the label outside the image | operator's instruction; the label is the id and the note |
| canvas | the bounding box of spine + both rails | no side whitespace; "clipped to the curve" |

The curve is as large as the image allows because the canvas aspect **is** the
drawn bounding box. A tall curve gets a tall plate; nothing is padded to a
square.

## Adding a plate

1. Add a row to `plates.json` with a fresh serial. The plates draw the saved
   curves from `workbench/real-curves.json`, so a row is `"kind": "seed"` plus
   the curve's `"name"`:

   ```json
   {"id": "amper-1-t-exp-c-0101", "descriptor": "amper", "variant": 1,
    "kind": "seed", "name": "amper", "note": "amper · saved curve"}
   ```

   The descriptor may contain hyphens; the `-t-exp-c-` marker is where the name
   is split. `node scripts/real_curves.mjs` rebuilds the curve data from the
   sandbox seed.
2. `width`, `plus`, `minus` and `profile` come from the curve's own record. If
   `|d·κ|` is too large, the width is halved until the base offset no longer
   folds; if it still folds at the 0.2% floor, the plate is drawn spine-only and
   says so.
3. Run:

```sh
node scripts/plates_export.mjs
```

It writes `svg/<id>.svg`, `plates/<id>.png` and `render.html`, prints the
distance, the fold margin, the pixel size and the bytes, and stamps 300 dpi. It
no longer writes `index.html`: the gallery is the Astro page at `/book`.

## Starred figures

The gallery's top section, **Framed Quintic symmetric figures**, is whatever the
operator stars in the lab. A browser cannot write a file,
so the bridge is a download: star a design in the lab, press **download
starred.json**, and save the file to `workbench/starred.json`. The next export
adds those plates under the top section. With no file, the section shows the
instruction rather than an error. The Astro gallery lists every star the moment
the file exists; a star whose PNG has not been exported yet says so on its card.

The section below it, **Simple framed symmetric central figures**, is the pair
in `plates.json` (cross and leaf). The 27 single curves from `plates.json` follow. The lab's picker offers the
full 88-curve set, including the 60 found curves; starring one promotes it to
the top section.

## What is not done

- **Clipping to the ink.** The curve's ends stop at the margin, not at a hand
  cut; the operator will trim where it matters.
- **Character offsets.** The rails are a constant distance; a varying width
  (a stroke that swells) is the later width-modulation track.
- **Labels.** Deliberately none on the image. If a plate needs a caption, it
  belongs in the book layout.
- **LibreOffice layout.** The plates are made for framing, not paged yet. A
  contact sheet with the trim size is the next step.
- **A final set.** `t` means temporary; the chosen plates get a stable set
  letter before print.

## The files

| path | what it is |
|---|---|
| `plates.json` | the manifest: id, source, offset share, note |
| `plates/*.png` | the images, 300 dpi |
| `svg/*.svg` | the same plates as SVG |
| `render.html` | the page the screenshots are taken from (generated) |

The gallery is not a generated file. It is `app/src/pages/book.astro`, reading
`plates.json` and `workbench/starred.json` on each request and serving the PNGs
through `/api/plate/<id>`. `workbench/plate_compose.js` writes every caption
once, for both the exporter and the page.
